transcript.text: Kanroji. Tell me about a mission where you failed — where someone died, or was gravely hurt, because of a choice you made. Don't tell me about the ones that went well. Tell me about the worst one. How did you handle it?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: It's... not an easy thing to talk about. There was a mission in a village that was being attacked by a particularly... enthusiastic Upper Rank. We were successful in driving them away, but... it came at a cost. A child, no more than 5 years old, was caught in the crossfire. I... could have been more careful with my positioning. I was... so focused on the Upper Rank that I didn't pay enough attention to my surroundings. It... it haunts me to this day.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: I see. And what was your immediate response when you realized the child was injured? Did you continue the pursuit, or did you stop to render aid?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer

I don't know how long I stood there, just... processing what had happened. When I finally snapped out of it, I... I rushed to the child's side. My... my movements were... uncoordinated, I was... so... emotional. I... I did the best I could to stabilize the injury, but... the damage was done. We... we took the child to the closest infirmary, but... it... it was too late. I... I stayed with them, held... their hand, the entire... way. I... failed them.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Your hesitation cost precious seconds. As a Hashira, you must maintain clarity even in the face of casualties. Tell me, what did you do after the mission was complete? Did you report this lapse in your official debriefing?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer

I was... so... overcome with... guilt. I... I know I... should have been... more... professional. I... I realize now that... I let my... emotions get in the way of... my duty. I... I should have... been more... clear, more... concise. I... I should have... taken full... responsibility for... my... mistake. I... I didn't... I... I... didn't handle it... well at all.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: I see. And what have you done since then to ensure such hesitation doesn't happen again? A Hashira cannot afford to freeze, no matter the circumstances. What specific training or mental discipline have you implemented?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I've... been working on... several... things. I... I started... meditating daily... to improve... my focus and... emotional control. I... I also... incorporated... more realistic... scenarios into... my training, to... simulate... high-pressure... situations. I... I've... been... working closely... with... other Hashira... to learn... from their... experiences and... decision-making processes. And... I... I've... taken... up... acting... lessons... to... better... understand... how to... manage... my... emotions... in... difficult... situations. I... I know... it may... seem... odd, but... it... helps... me... to... 'live'... through... different... scenarios... and... practice... remaining... composed. I... I... am... also... more... intentional... about... maintaining... situational... awareness... during... missions... to... prevent... future... oversights.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Acting lessons. An... unconventional approach. But if it helps you maintain composure when lives are at stake, then it has merit. Tell me this: when you close your eyes at night, do you still see that child's face? And if so, how do you prevent that image from paralyzing you again?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Yes... I... do. It's... still... there. It... haunts my... dreams... and... sometimes... my... waking... moments. But... I... I don't... let it... paralyze... me anymore. I... I... remember... that... child... every... time... I... go... into... a... mission... now. It... it... reminds... me... of... why... we... do... what... we... do. It... drives... me... to... be... better... and... more... careful. I... I... dedicate... each... mission... to... them... in... my... own... way... as... a... promise... to... do... everything... in... my... power... to... protect... others. It... it... doesn't... make... the... pain... go... away... but... it... gives... me... a... purpose... to... focus... on... instead... of... the... guilt. And... it... helps... me... to... stay... vigilant... and... determined... to... prevent... such... a... tragedy... from... happening... again.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Good. That is the proper way to carry such weight. The guilt will never leave you—nor should it. But you've learned to let it sharpen your focus rather than shatter your resolve. That is the mark of growth. Continue your training, and continue to honor that child's memory through your actions. You are dismissed.
